Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education
Our personal, social, health and economic (PSHE) curriculum supports our White House Academy pupils to be healthy, safe and prepared for modern life.
Our PSHE curriculum offers both explicit and implicit learning opportunities, tailored to each stage of development as our students progress through primary school. It builds upon the foundational skills acquired during the Early Years Foundation stage (EYFS) and helps students develop effective relationships, take on greater personal responsibility, and manage their personal safety, including online safety.
We aim to guide students through the physical and emotional changes they experience during puberty, and introduce them to the broader world, empowering them to actively contribute to their communities.

Music
Our music provision at White House Academy is designed to ensure that every child is taught how to play an instrument before they leave our academy.
Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. A high quality music education should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement. As pupils progress, they should develop a critical engagement with music, allowing them to compose, and to listen with discrimination to the best in the musical canon.

Physical Education
Throughout their time at White House Academy, children will participate in a variety of different sports, including dance and swimming, in order to master basic skills and movements such as running, jumping, throwing and catching, while also developing their balance, agility and co-ordination. The children will engage in various team games where they will develop and use their skills and knowledge to plan simple tactics for attacking and defending. Our PE curriculum aims to not only improve physical fitness and promote healthy lifestyles, but also to improve children’s teamwork, focus and leadership skills.

Geography
At White House Academy, our Geography curriculum is strategically designed to align with our core educational values of global awareness and critical thinking.
We are dedicated to cultivating in our students a profound grasp of the world and the essential skills for critical thinking, thereby equipping them to become active, informed global citizens. Our comprehensive teaching approach integrates geography into our array of literary texts, allowing students not only to absorb foundational geographical knowledge but also to develop practical skills. This curriculum design enhances their comprehension of the texts while concurrently fostering a deeper appreciation for the diversity of places and cultures that enrich our global community.
Our approach seeks to instil an enduring passion for geography that transcends the classroom, nurturing a lifelong curiosity about the world and instilling the critical thinking skills indispensable for navigating its multifaceted complexities. In this endeavour, students gain both declarative knowledge about geographical facts and procedural skills in map reading, research, and analytical thinking.

Art
Our art curriculum is designed to develop the children’s knowledge and skills in drawing, painting and sculpture. They develop their techniques while using a range of materials such as pencil, charcoal, paint and clay. Through studying famous works of a variety of artists, children are encouraged to develop the language to identify and explore many formal elements of art. They use this knowledge and key skills to plan and develop their own pieces of artwork.

Computing
Developing computational thinking in students from an early age will help them to understand and contribute to the community they will live in as adults. At White House Academy, our teachers will ensure that our teaching focusses on the learners' development rather than technology. This program will develop our students' understanding of algorithms, how the algorithms are implemented as programs on digital devices, and that programs execute by following precise and unambiguous instructions; create and debug simple programs; improve computer literacy and how to use the internet securely
A high-quality computing education equips pupils to use computational thinking and deepens the links with mathematics, science and design and technology, and provides insights into both natural and artificial systems. The core of computing is computer science, in which pupils are taught the principles of information and computation, how digital systems work and how to put this knowledge to use through programming.

English
Our approach to English
Our English curriculum is carefully crafted to empower students with the skills and knowledge they need to excel in the world of literature and language.
Our English curriculum is driven by a canon of high-quality texts. We understand that reading is more than just words on a page – it's about comprehension, fluency, and vocabulary enrichment. Through our whole-class reading lessons, students engage in immersive reading experiences. This not only enhances their reading fluency but also nurtures their confidence in expressing themselves through language.
To deepen their understanding of the texts, we use a targeted approach that focusses on the knowledge children need to fully comprehend the book at hand. We encourage critical thinking and analytical skills, teaching students to answer questions using the "I, we, you" model. Vocabulary development is also a significant part of our reading curriculum, ensuring that students expand their lexicon and become more articulate communicators.
We recognise the importance of building a strong foundation. That's why we begin with sentence work, focusing on the fundamental building blocks of writing. This approach ensures that our students grasp the essential elements before moving on to more complex writing tasks.
We believe in the importance of nurturing the writing process. Our students learn the value of planning, drafting, and revising, turning initial ideas into polished works of art. This iterative approach allows them to refine their writing over time, transforming it from good to exceptional.Our students are encouraged to identify both purpose and audience for each piece of writing they undertake. This emphasis on intentionality ensures that their writing has a real-world context, making it a meaningful and authentic endeavour.
Grammar is not taught in isolation but within the context of writing. Our approach ensures that students understand how grammar functions in real-world writing scenarios. Daily quizzes reinforce these concepts, helping children store this vital knowledge in their long-term memory. Explicit instruction in handwriting and spelling is a cornerstone of our writing curriculum.
Through teacher modelling, students learn by example, witnessing how experienced writers craft their work. This hands-on guidance inspires and informs our young writers, showing them the path to success.

History
Our history curriculum at White House Academy carefully links with class texts, ensuring a broad and in-depth understanding of the past.
We provide a coherent and chronological narrative, studying significant events and individuals from global, British, and local perspectives. Students explore recurring themes, causes, effects, and changes in history, and answer thought-provoking 'big questions' each term. Our curriculum aims to inspire a love for learning about the past, develop critical thinking skills, and foster historical empathy, empowering students to shape a better future based on the lessons of history.

Maths
We take a mastery approach to the teaching and learning of mathematics. Fundamentally, this rests on the belief that all children can – and, indeed, must – be successful in the study of mathematics.
We do not accept that ‘some people cannot do maths’; we do not accept that mathematical study is boring or unnecessary; we do not accept that prior attainment should limit what a child is capable of learning. Mathematics is for everyone.
We aim for all children to move together through the learning to avoid gaps in understanding from forming. Children who do not meet the learning objective for a lesson are identified in the lesson and are given a same-day intervention where possible to ensure that they are ready to move on to the next day’s learning.

EYFS
EYFS Curriculum Overview
The key formative years of childhood are short – therefore the quality of the learning and teaching experience is of great importance. The vital skills and concepts formed in the Early Years help children make sense of their knowledge and understanding. They are the foundations upon which the quality of later learning and development depends.
Reception is the crucial first year of your child's formal education. In Reception, we follow the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework. Our curriculum is designed to provide a holistic and engaging learning experience that supports your child's social, emotional, physical, and intellectual development.
In Reception, we prioritise the prime areas of learning, which are communication and language, physical development, and personal, social, and emotional development. These areas form the foundation upon which all other learning is built. Through a range of interactive activities, play-based learning, and meaningful experiences, we nurture your child's language skills, physical abilities, and social interactions, enabling them to develop confidence, independence, and positive relationships.
We also place a strong emphasis on the specific areas of learning, which are literacy, mathematics, understanding the world, and expressive arts and design. Through engaging and purposeful activities, we help your child develop early literacy skills, such as reading, writing, and communication. In mathematics, we encourage exploration, problem-solving, and number recognition, fostering a solid understanding of basic mathematical concepts.
Understanding the world encompasses a range of experiences, including exploring the natural environment, reading stories and learning about different cultures and traditions. Through hands-on investigations, visits, and discussions, we ignite curiosity and develop your child's knowledge and understanding of the world around them.
Expressive arts and design provide opportunities for your child to express their creativity, imagination, and emotions through various art forms, music, movement, and role-play. These experiences enhance their communication skills, self-expression, and aesthetic appreciation.
Our curriculum is carefully planned to ensure progression, catering to each child's unique needs and interests. We utilise continuous observation, assessment, and feedback to tailor our teaching approaches and provide targeted support to ensure your child's ongoing progress.
At White House Academy, we value strong partnerships with parents and carers. We encourage open communication and involvement in your child's learning journey. We provide regular updates on your child's progress and offer opportunities for parents and carers to contribute to their learning experiences.

Design and Technology
Design and technology at White House Academy is an inspiring, rigorous and practical subject. Using creativity and imagination, pupils design and make products that solve real and relevant problems within a variety of contexts, considering their own and others’ needs, wants and values. They acquire a broad range of subject knowledge and draw on disciplines such as mathematics, science, computing and art.
Pupils learn how to take risks, becoming resourceful, innovative, enterprising and capable citizens.
Through the evaluation of past and present design and technology, they develop a critical understanding of its impact on daily life and the wider world. High-quality design and technology education makes an essential contribution to the creativity, culture, wealth and well-being of the nation.

Phonics
Our phonics curriculum aims to develop confident, fluent readers by building foundational skills in decoding and recognising words. Our school uses the Sounds Right programme to deliver phonics instruction effectively, ensuring consistency and a structured approach to learning. The Sounds Right approach systematically introduces sounds, blending, and segmenting strategies, which are crucial for early literacy development. (What is Sounds-Write? - Sounds-Write)
By using 'Sounds Right,' we provide our students with an engaging and interactive learning experience emphasising repetition and progression. This programme helps children master phonemic awareness, understand the relationships between sounds and letters, and apply their learning to reading and writing activities. Its structure allows students to build on their skills gradually, moving from simple sounds to more complex phonemes as their confidence grows.
A key strength of 'Sounds Right' is its focus on multisensory learning. Through actions, visuals, and auditory cues, students engage with phonics in multiple ways, accommodating diverse learning styles. This multimodal approach ensures that all learners, regardless of ability, are supported in their journey towards reading fluency.
Our phonics curriculum is also tailored to identify and support individual needs. Regular assessments are embedded to monitor progress, allowing for timely intervention where necessary. This ensures that all children can keep up and that gaps in learning are addressed early. The goal is to ensure that every child can access the full curriculum and become an enthusiastic, capable reader.
Ultimately, our approach to phonics lays the foundation for a lifetime of literacy. By focusing on systematic instruction, engagement, and tailored support, we aim to give every student the skills they need to succeed in their reading journey, setting them up for further learning and a deep love of books and language.

Pupil Representation
At White House Academy, we believe that students should have a voice in shaping their educational experience, and that's why we have established a vibrant and inclusive Pupil Representation program. These roles empower students to take an active role in making our school a better place.
Here's a brief overview some of these roles role:
​Pupil Parliament: Our Pupil Parliament represents the voice of our students. They meet regularly to discuss important school matters, propose ideas for improvements, and work with school staff to make positive changes.
Pupil Librarians: Our Pupil Librarians are passionate about promoting literacy and a love for reading. They assist in the library, recommend books, and create a welcoming reading environment for all students.
Eco Warriors: Committed to environmental sustainability, our Eco Warriors are responsible for raising awareness about eco-friendly practices. They initiate projects to reduce waste, conserve resources, and make our school a greener place.
Play Leaders: Play Leaders are dedicated to ensuring that everyone has a safe and enjoyable playtime. They organise games and activities, mediate conflicts, and promote inclusivity and kindness on the playground.
Our Pupil Representation program empowers students to develop leadership skills, learn about democracy and decision-making, and contribute positively to our school community. We encourage active participation and engagement from all students.

Pastoral Care
Our Pastoral Support Programme
At White House Academy, we want everyone involved with our school to feel well supported. We believe that good pastoral support focusses on nurturing the individual needs of each child. We aim to build trusting and empathic relationships with all our pupils and their families.
Our Inclusion Team is made up of dedicated professionals. This includes our Senior Leadership Team and a team of therapists. Together our team works with students so they can lead fulfilling and balanced lives at school and beyond.
All our staff model to students how to look after themselves and others; encouraging them to seek help, support or advice whenever they need it.
Pastoral care underpins personal development and we know from experience that with outstanding pastoral care, students feel they belong and their self-esteem is able to flourish because they feel valued and cared for.
Supporting the pastoral needs of pupils sometimes involves working with external agencies. In these situations we ensure that a confidential, professional, non-judgemental and sensitive service is provided.
White House Academy’s Pastoral Support includes:
· Range of academic interventions organised by the SENDCO
· Art therapist and play therapist
· Mental health support team
· External agencies such as; Social Services, Police, Health Professionals, Education Welfare Service, Doctors and nurses.
· Focused nurture provision
· Full time behaviour mentor
· Speech and language support
· Lunch and break clubs for children who struggle in larger groups
· Breakfast and after school clubs
If you would like to find out more about any of these pastoral support services, please contact the school office.
